sections.title: Understanding the Problem
points: The application displays stock prices and manages customer orders. External trading infrastructure accepts orders and reports executions.
A displayed price, a submitted order, an external acknowledgement, and an execution are different records with different timing.

sections.title: Functional Requirements
points: Users can view live stock prices. They can create and cancel market or limit orders.
Users can list their orders and inspect the latest recorded state.
The system integrates with an external exchange interface. Designing an exchange matching engine is outside this scope.

sections.title: Non-functional Requirements
points: Order state needs strong consistency and durability. The target is less than 200 ms for normal price updates and order requests.
The scenario has 20 million daily users and about five trades per user. Repeated requests must not create unintended orders.
Minimize expensive external feed connections. Scale popular-symbol delivery separately from order processing.

sections.title: Core Entities
points: User identifies the authenticated customer. Symbol identifies a traded stock.
Order contains its owner, symbol, side, quantity, type, limit price where applicable, and lifecycle state.
Execution records a fill quantity, price, external identifier, and time. External order metadata maps provider IDs to local orders.
Quote contains symbol, price, sequence information, and timestamp. Account and Position records are needed if portfolio management enters scope.

sections.title: API
points: GET /symbol/{name} returns a price snapshot. A subscription request lists the symbols for live updates.
POST /order creates an order with a stable client request ID. Represent currency with a defined exact numeric representation.
GET /orders lists the authenticated user's orders. DELETE /order/{id} requests cancellation of an eligible order.
A cancellation request does not prove cancellation. The order can fill before the external system confirms the request.

sections.title: 1) Live prices
points: Direct client polling of the exchange creates redundant external calls. An internal Symbol Price Processor can share the upstream feed.
The processor updates the Symbol Cache. The initial internal design lets clients poll the Symbol Service for current values.
The improved Symbol Service sends an initial snapshot and later updates through SSE. Clients no longer poll for every change.
Include timestamps or sequence information. A client must not replace a newer displayed price with an older update.

flows.title: Subscribe to current prices and live updates
steps: The Symbol Price Processor receives the external price feed and updates the Symbol Cache.
The client requests a symbol subscription through the API Gateway.
The Symbol Service reads the current prices from the cache and sends that snapshot.
It keeps an SSE connection open. Later processor updates reach the client through that connection.

sections.title: 2) Orders
points: Direct client submission leaves order tracking on an unreliable device. A server-side Order Service owns the durable local record.
A queued dispatcher can absorb bursts, but queue delay can exceed the order target. The source selects synchronous dispatch through a gateway.
The Order Service stores a pending order before contacting the exchange through the Order Dispatch Gateway.
After acknowledgement, it stores the external order ID and marks the order submitted. The Trade Processor later applies execution reports.
Stable client order IDs support recovery after a lost response. Local acceptance must not claim that the order has filled.

flows.title: Submit an order through the dispatch gateway
steps: The client submits order parameters and a stable request ID to the Order Service.
The service validates the authenticated request. It stores a pending order in the Orders DB.
It sends the order through the Order Dispatch Gateway to the external exchange.
The exchange returns its order ID. The service records that ID and the submitted state.
The service returns the confirmed submission result. A timeout triggers reconciliation instead of an unchecked second order.
Later execution reports update the order through the Trade Processor. Submission is not proof of a fill.

sections.title: 1) Scale price delivery
points: The Symbol Price Processor publishes updates through Redis Pub/Sub. Each Symbol Service instance subscribes only to symbols its clients need.
One server subscription can serve many local clients. Remove the upstream subscription when that server has no interested clients.
Coalesce display updates if the product only needs the latest price. Keep authoritative execution events separate from that lossy path.
Bound buffers for slow clients. After reconnecting, send a fresh snapshot instead of an unlimited backlog of old prices.

flows.title: Distribute a price through shared subscriptions
steps: A Symbol Service instance records the symbols requested by its connected clients.
It subscribes to each needed Redis Pub/Sub channel once for that server.
The Symbol Price Processor updates the latest quote and publishes the change to the symbol's channel.
Interested Symbol Service instances receive the update. Each sends it to the relevant local clients.
When no local client needs a symbol, the server removes that subscription. Reconnecting clients receive a fresh snapshot.

sections.title: 2) Track order updates
points: Partition the Orders DB by user ID. Keep a separate mapping from external order ID to local order ID and user ID.
The Trade Processor uses that mapping to find the correct database partition and order. It applies each execution report once.
Model pending, submitted, partially filled, filled, pending cancellation, cancelled, and rejected states explicitly.
Preserve cumulative fills and external report IDs. Reconcile missing acknowledgements or reports with the external provider.
Publish customer-facing changes after committing state. A notification must not announce a fill that the system failed to record.

flows.title: Apply an external execution report
steps: The Trade Processor receives a report containing the external order ID.
It queries the External Order Metadata DB for the corresponding local order ID and user ID.
The user ID identifies the Orders DB partition. The processor loads the order from that partition.
It deduplicates the execution report and updates the cumulative fill and order state.
It commits the update before notifying the customer. An unresolved mapping or missing report enters reconciliation.

sections.title: 3) Order consistency
points: Store pending intent before submission. After an uncertain response, query the provider using the stable client order ID.
The Order Clean-up Job checks unresolved pending and cancellation states. It repairs local records from confirmed external outcomes.
A timeout does not prove rejection. An unverified retry can create a second order.
If funds and positions enter scope, reserve the required amount atomically with order acceptance. Fills consume only their corresponding reservation.
Cancellation or rejection releases only the unfilled remainder. Keep transition history so audits can reconstruct what occurred.

flows.title: Resolve cancellation racing a fill
steps: The Order Service records a cancellation request as pending cancellation.
It submits the request through the Order Dispatch Gateway using the provider's order ID.
The Trade Processor continues applying valid execution reports. A cancellation request cannot undo an already completed fill.
After external confirmation, the service closes only the unfilled remainder.
If the response is uncertain, the Order Clean-up Job queries external status and repairs the local record.

sections.title: Final Design
points: The Symbol Price Processor maintains the cache and shared price channels. Symbol Service instances send relevant updates to clients.
The Order Service stores intent and submits through the Order Dispatch Gateway. The Trade Processor updates orders using external-ID mappings.
The Order Clean-up Job reconciles uncertain outcomes. Stable identifiers and durable transitions support retries and recovery.
